profile_text.body:
Speechmatics is a Cambridge, GB company founded in 2006 that builds speech-to-text APIs. Its site describes the APIs as made for real conversations rather than clean demos, and says they handle accents, multiple speakers, and multilingual speech. The company's tracked product sits in the Voice and Audio category, noted for speech-to-text, real-time translation, accent-agnostic processing, UK hosting, and GDPR.

The site describes sub-second, speaker-aware speech-to-text and text-to-speech across 55+ languages, reached through a flexible API and native integrations for AI voice agents. It says a single model transcribes 55+ languages even when speakers switch languages mid-conversation, and that one voice AI API powers live captions, voice agents, meeting notes, and contact center analytics. Speechmatics names two models: Melia 1, a multilingual speech-to-text model with code-switching across 55+ languages, available in production preview starting with batch transcription, and Linden, a speech-to-text model built for voice agents and available through LiveKit Inference with no separate API key, account, or invoice. The company states that on Arabic and English Melia 1 runs at less than half the mixed error rate of the next best model, and that on Mandarin and Tamil it switches more accurately than anything else it tested. Its site also compares 12 text-to-speech APIs, including ElevenLabs, Google Cloud, Amazon Polly, and Speechmatics.
